help.title: Ayuda y líneas de crisis
help.subtitle: No estás sole. Encuentra apoyo inmediato aquí.
help.meta_description: Líneas de crisis y servicios de apoyo LGBTQIA+ gratuitos y anónimos en todo el mundo. No estás sole.
help.emergency_body: Llama a emergencias ahora mismo: 112 (UE) o 911 (EE.UU./CA). Cada segundo cuenta.
help.disclaimer: Queer Guide no sustituye la ayuda profesional.
help.no_results: Ninguna línea coincide con estos filtros. Prueba "Todos los países" o consulta los directorios internacionales.
help.error_body: En peligro inmediato, llama a tu número de emergencias local: 112 (UE) o 911 (EE.UU./CA).
help.reveal_aria: Haz clic en cualquier parte para volver a mostrar la página
help.hidden_hint: Página oculta. Haz clic en cualquier parte para mostrarla.
help.expect_1: You'll hear a short greeting. You don't have to give your name.
help.expect_2: You can hang up at any time. You can call back as often as you need.
help.expect_3: Free hotlines in DE/AT/CH don't appear on itemized phone bills.
help.expect_4: If you can't speak, ask for text or chat — most hotlines offer it.
help.self_help_desc: Short techniques you can use while you wait, or instead of a call if you're not ready.
help.breathing_1: Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds.
help.breathing_3: Breathe out through your mouth for 8 seconds.
help.grounding_intro: Name, out loud or in your head:
help.safety_plan_desc: A short written plan you can pull up when things get bad — your warning signs, coping steps, people to call, and reasons to live.
help.report_aria: Report a problem with this hotline
help.report_desc: Thanks for helping keep this list accurate. Reports are reviewed by our team.
help.closed_no_alt: Esta línea está cerrada ahora mismo y no tenemos ninguna otra abierta para este país. Si hay peligro inmediato, usa el número de emergencia de arriba.
help.directories_subtitle: Son directorios y organizaciones de derivación: sitios web, no líneas telefónicas directas.
help.helping_body: Si estás escuchando a alguien en crisis: quédate con esa persona, toma en serio lo que dice y no la dejes sola. No necesitas tener las respuestas. Llamad juntos a una línea, o llama tú para preguntar qué hacer.
help.know_the_law_body: Si es seguro vivir abiertamente, buscar atención médica o denunciar un delito depende de dónde estés. Comprueba la situación legal antes de actuar.
help.link_unavailable: Sitio web no disponible ahora mismo: se está volviendo a comprobar.
help.no_country_body: Elige un país arriba y te mostraremos la mejor línea. Todas nuestras líneas aparecen abajo.
help.no_country_title: No hemos podido determinar dónde estás
help.no_lines_body: Si estás en peligro ahora mismo, llama a emergencias: 112 (UE) o 911 (EE. UU./CA).
help.no_lines_title: No se ha podido cargar el directorio
help.no_police_policy: Esta línea se compromete a no contactar nunca con la policía ni con los servicios de emergencia sin tu petición explícita.
help.org_coverage: Este directorio está lejos de ser completo. Si falta un grupo en el que confías, dínoslo. Un resultado vacío significa que no tenemos constancia, no que no exista ayuda.
help.phone_only: Solo por teléfono, según nuestros datos.
help.phone_only_with_site: Solo por teléfono, según nuestros datos. Su web puede ofrecer chat o correo electrónico.
help.reports_police_warning: Esta línea puede contactar con la policía o los servicios de emergencia sin tu consentimiento.
help.scope_all: Líneas de todos los países registrados.
help.scope_dialog_desc: Las líneas se ordenan por el país al que atienden. Los directorios internacionales siguen visibles elijas lo que elijas.
help.support_orgs_body: Centros comunitarios y asociaciones que ofrecen apoyo presencial.

milestones.pageDescription: Hitos que marcaron la vida LGBTQ+: levantamientos, leyes, retrocesos. Con fechas y fuentes.
milestones.metaDescription: Hitos de la historia LGBTQ+: levantamientos, despenalizaciones, matrimonio igualitario y retrocesos — con fechas y fuentes, en todo el mundo.
milestones.empty: Ningún hito coincide con estos filtros.

sections.sameYearNote: [ES] What was happening in other countries the same year.

hidden-lives.title: [ES] Hidden lives
hidden-lives.intro: Antes de 1800, la vida queer sobrevivió a la sombra de la ley y la iglesia. Lo que conserva el registro es sobre todo persecución: juicios, ejecuciones, edictos. Junto a ello, destellos raros de amor y comunidad que los sobrevivieron.

empire-criminalization.title: [ES] Empire & criminalization
empire-criminalization.intro: [ES] Colonial empires exported sodomy laws across the globe in the 19th century, while a few states — revolutionary France first among them — quietly removed their own. Much of today's legal map was drawn in this era.

birth-of-movement.title: [ES] Birth of a movement
birth-of-movement.intro: [ES] Between the 1860s and the early 1930s the first words, organizations and campaigns emerged: Kertbeny coined 'homosexual', Hirschfeld founded the first gay rights organization, and Berlin briefly became the queer capital of the world.

destruction.title: [ES] Destruction
destruction.intro: [ES] Fascism destroyed the first movement. The Nazis burned Hirschfeld's institute, tightened Paragraph 175 and deported thousands of gay men to concentration camps. Remembering this era is part of why this timeline exists.

homophile-years.title: [ES] The homophile years
homophile-years.intro: Tras la guerra, pequeños grupos «homófilos» reconstruyeron en silencio: Mattachine, las Daughters of Bilitis, Arcadie, el COC. Cambiaron radicalidad por respetabilidad mientras seguían las redadas y las purgas.

liberation.title: [ES] Liberation
liberation.intro: [ES] Stonewall in 1969 turned decades of quiet organizing into open revolt. Pride marches spread worldwide, homosexuality left the psychiatric manuals, and the first anti-discrimination laws were won.

aids-crisis.title: [ES] The AIDS crisis
aids-crisis.intro: Una generación fue diezmada mientras los gobiernos miraban a otro lado. El duelo de la epidemia forjó el activismo combativo que transformó por igual la medicina y la política queer: ACT UP, campañas por el acceso al tratamiento.

recognition.title: [ES] Recognition
recognition.intro: [ES] From the first registered partnerships to the Netherlands opening marriage in 2001, courts and parliaments began recognizing queer lives: decriminalization accelerated and trans rights entered the legal mainstream.

equality-wave.title: [ES] The equality wave
equality-wave.intro: [ES] The 2010s brought marriage equality to dozens of countries on every continent, landmark court rulings from the United States to India, and unprecedented queer visibility in public life.

backlash-now.title: [ES] Backlash & now
backlash-now.intro: [ES] Progress continues — and so does organized backlash: 'LGBT-free zones', anti-trans legislation and new criminalization drives. The timeline is still being written.

sources.title: [ES] Where this data comes from
sources.lede: [ES] We publish the legal status of LGBTQ+ people in every country and territory we cover. This page says who recorded it, how often we refresh it, how much of it we actually hold, and the questions it cannot answer.
sources.metaTitle: [ES] Where our LGBTQ+ rights data comes from
sources.metaDescription: [ES] The sources, refresh cadence, coverage and known limits behind the legal status we publish for every country and territory.

section.limits: [ES] What this data cannot tell you

kicker.score: [ES] How it is built, and what it hides

coverage.status: [ES] Countries with a recorded legal status

body.source: Todo estatus legal de este sitio procede de la ILGA World Database, el conjunto de datos de referencia que mantiene la International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association. Eso abarca criminalización, reconocimiento de la pareja, protección antidiscriminación, reconocimiento de género, terapias de conversión e integridad corporal intersex.
body.refresh: [ES] We re-import it nightly. Where a country page shows an "Updated" date, that is the date ILGA last revised that record, not the date we fetched it.
body.unscored: [ES] The unscored rows are uninhabited or near-uninhabited territories with no ILGA entry. We list them as "not scored" rather than giving them a default, because a default would read as a measurement.
body.scoreHow: [ES] The score runs 0–100. It starts at 50 and moves up or down as each recorded right is added: decriminalisation and marriage weigh heaviest, then anti-discrimination protections, hate-crime law, adoption, legal gender recognition and a conversion-therapy ban.
body.scoreLimit: [ES] Because it opens at 50 and adds from there, a country we hold almost nothing about lands mid-scale rather than reading as unknown. A middling score can mean middling rights or thin data, and the number cannot tell you which.
body.scoreLens: [ES] It is also a single number for very different lives. Protections are recorded separately for sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics, and those four rarely move together — a country can protect sexual orientation thoroughly and gender identity not at all. Read the per-right breakdown on a country page rather than the score alone.
body.scoreNotSafety: [ES] The score describes law on paper. It is not a safety rating, and it says nothing about enforcement, policing or how welcome you will be made to feel.

limits.national: Es nacional. Donde los derechos varían por estado o provincia, como en Estados Unidos, Indonesia, Nigeria y México, una sola cifra nacional promedia esa diferencia.
limits.enforcement: [ES] It records statutes, not enforcement. A law that is rarely applied and a law applied constantly look identical here.
limits.trans: [ES] Several facts that matter most to trans travellers are not in this dataset at all: bathroom and facility access, how identity documents are treated at borders, and access to gender-affirming healthcare.
limits.personal: [ES] It knows nothing about you. Your citizenship, residency, gender marker and relationship status all change what applies, and we hold none of them.
limits.corrections: [ES] If something here is wrong, tell us — corrections to the underlying record should also go to ILGA, who maintain it.

lens.title: [ES] Who the law protects
lens.noData: [ES] We hold no recorded legal status for this country or territory.

story.title: Cómo empezó
story.p1: Encontrar un bar queer-friendly no debería costar un grupo de chat, tres hilos de foro y un salto de fe. Empezamos Queer Guide porque nos cansamos de adivinar qué espacios eran seguros de verdad, y cuáles solo ponían un arcoíris en el logo en junio.
story.p2: Una lista personal de sitios de confianza se convirtió en un directorio global: verificado por la comunidad, construido sobre experiencias reales, gratis. Viajando en solitario, mudándote de ciudad o buscando dónde estar un viernes por la noche: empieza aquí.

hanky.title: El código
hanky.intro: Un pañuelo en el bolsillo trasero señalaba un interés concreto: el bolsillo izquierdo para el lado activo, el derecho para el receptivo. Documentado tal como se publicó en los años 80; los significados variaban según la ciudad y la década.
hanky.safeMode: La tabla de colores cubre prácticas sexuales explícitas y está oculta mientras el Modo Seguro está activado.
hanky.gateBody: La tabla de colores nombra prácticas sexuales explícitas. Confirma que tienes 18 años o más para leerla.
hanky.disclaimer: Referencia histórica, no un respaldo de ninguna práctica. Circularon docenas de colores más; no hay dos listas publicadas que coincidan del todo.

fourLines.title: [ES] Four lines
fourLines.caption: [ES] Gender identity, gender expression, sex assigned at birth and attraction are four separate lines. Pick a stop on each. Nothing is stored or sent.
fourLines.summary: [ES] A transit map with four lines: gender identity drawn as two independent services on one corridor, gender expression, sex assigned at birth as a terminus that runs on to nothing, and attraction. They meet at a single interchange.
fourLines.readout: [ES] Where you are on each line
fourLines.tableCaption: [ES] Every line on the map and the stops it carries

help.identityWoman: [ES] Who you know yourself to be. This runs independently of the line below it. You can be a lot of both, a little of both, or neither.
help.identityMan: [ES] The second rail on the same corridor. Answering this one does not subtract from the one above.
help.expression: [ES] How you present: clothes, voice, hair, the way you carry yourself. Stops, not a scale. Nothing here is halfway between two others.
help.assigned: [ES] What someone wrote down when you were born. It is a starting point on the record, which is why this line stops instead of running on to the others.
help.attraction: [ES] Who you are drawn to. Who you are and who you are drawn to are separate lines. That is the whole point of the map.

consentFlow.title: [ES] The line that stops
consentFlow.caption: [ES] Consent as a route with signals, one speed restriction and no final destination. It loops back to the check-in and stays there. Not a legal test; the law differs by country.
consentFlow.summary: [ES] A branching line. Asking without an answer, and anything that is not a clear yes, end at buffer stops. Capacity is a hatched speed-restriction section rather than a yes/no signal. The line does not terminate in approval. It loops back to a check-in signal that can be answered again at any time.
consentFlow.tableCaption: [ES] Every stop on the line, and where it leads
consentFlow.hint: [ES] Select any stop to light up the route that reaches it.

node.start: [ES] You want to do something with someone
node.clearYes: [ES] Was the answer a clear yes?
node.capacity: [ES] Speed restriction: can everyone actually decide?

note.asked: [ES] Out loud, or in a way you have both already agreed reads as asking.
note.notAsked: [ES] Not objecting is not agreeing. The line does not start here.
note.clearYes: [ES] Theirs, not one you talked them into.
note.notAYes: [ES] Anything that is not a yes is a no. This is the end of the line.
note.capacity: [ES] Drink, drugs, exhaustion, being half asleep. Not a switch. If you cannot tell, you do not have an answer yet.
note.checkin: [ES] The signal you come back to. Agreeing earlier is not agreeing now.
note.stopNow: [ES] Anyone can stop anything at any point, for no reason. Then look after each other.
note.go: [ES] And back to the check-in, which is why this line is a loop.
